# Tutorial: Create a Thumbnail Function Invoked by Amazon S3

## Overview

In this tutorial, Amazon S3 invokes a Lambda Event Function when an image file is added to the source bucket. The function creates a thumbnail version of the image and outputs it to a different Amazon S3 bucket. You can complete the tutorial using the AWS CLI or the AWS Management Console, and you can write the function in Python or Node.js.

Running commands requires a command line terminal or shell. Some Bash CLI commands, such as zip, are not supported by the built-in terminals in Windows. If you use Windows, the Windows Subsystem for Linux provides a Windows-integrated version of Ubuntu and Bash, which you can use to work around this limitation.

## Buckets and test image

You need two buckets. The source bucket is the one that images are uploaded to. The destination bucket stores the resized thumbnail. The source bucket name must be globally unique and must follow Amazon S3 bucket naming rules, which allow only lower case letters, numbers, dots, and hyphens. The destination bucket name must be the source bucket name followed by -resized.

Create both the destination bucket and the Lambda Event Function in the same AWS Region as the source bucket. The source bucket must also contain a test image to confirm the function operates correctly. The test image can be any JPG or PNG file.

## Permissions and execution role

An execution role is an IAM role that grants a Lambda Event Function permission to access AWS services and resources. The permissions policy gives the function read and write permissions for Amazon S3 buckets and allows it to write to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The permissions policy is attached to the execution role.

The role also has a trust policy. It gives the service principal lambda.amazonaws.com permission to call sts:AssumeRole, which allows Lambda to use the role's permissions. In this tutorial the function uses the LambdaS3Role execution role.

## Deployment package

A deployment package contains the function code and its dependencies. The function code uses a separate library for image resizing. The files and dependency folders must be at the root of the .zip file.

In the Lambda console, you first create a basic Hello world function and then replace its code by uploading the .zip file. The function is named CreateThumbnail and uses the x86_64 architecture.

### Node.js

The Node.js function uses the sharp library. The latest version of sharp (0.33) is not compatible with Lambda, so install version 0.32.6 for this tutorial. The function sets the thumbnail width to 200 pixels, and the resize operation sets the height automatically to maintain aspect ratio. The function only supports jpg and png image types. If the image type is unsupported, it returns without resizing.

### Python

The Python function uses the Pillow library, which contains C/C++ code. The pip options --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 and --only-binary=:all: install Pillow with pre-compiled binaries compatible with Amazon Linux 2. These binaries make the deployment package work in the Lambda execution environment regardless of the local build machine's OS and architecture.

The Lambda Python runtime includes a version of the Boto3 SDK. Even so, it is recommended to add all function dependencies to the deployment package.

## Configuring the trigger

For the function to run when an image is uploaded to the source bucket, you must configure a trigger. The S3 trigger invokes the function every time an object is created in the bucket. Configure the trigger only on the source bucket. A function that creates objects in the bucket that invokes it can be invoked continuously in a loop, which can result in unexpected charges to the AWS account. For this reason, using the same S3 bucket for input and output is not recommended.

When you create a trigger, the Lambda console automatically creates a resource-based policy. A resource-based policy statement gives other AWS services permission to invoke the function. If you use the CLI instead, the aws lambda add-permission command gives Amazon S3 permission to invoke the function. This policy allows Amazon S3 to invoke the function only for actions on the source bucket.

It is best practice to specify in resource-based policies that the bucket must belong to your account. If a bucket is deleted, another AWS account can create a bucket with the same ARN. The notification configuration then sends a notification to the function every time a new object is added.

## Testing

A Lambda event is a JSON-formatted document containing data for the function to process. The event sent by S3 contains the bucket name, bucket ARN, and object key.

Run the dummy event test before testing by uploading an image. Invocation type RequestResponse invokes the function synchronously. The cli-binary-format option is required with version 2 of the AWS CLI. After the dummy event test, the destination bucket contains a resized image.

For the second test, upload an image to the source bucket. The Lambda function is automatically invoked when an image is added to the source bucket. After both tests, the destination bucket contains two resized files.

## Cleanup

Deleting unused AWS resources prevents unnecessary charges.

**Python.** The function uses the Pillow library, which contains C/C++ code. The pip options --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 and --only-binary=:all: install Pillow with pre-compiled binaries compatible with Amazon Linux 2. Only when these options are used do the pre-compiled binaries make the deployment package work in the Lambda execution environment regardless of the local build machine's OS and architecture. The Lambda Python runtime includes a version of the Boto3 SDK. Even so, it is recommended to add all function dependencies to the deployment package even if included in the runtime.

## Create the function

Name the function CreateThumbnail, use the x86_64 architecture, and use the LambdaS3Role execution role. Upload the .zip file to replace the Hello world code.

## Configure the trigger

A trigger must be configured for the function to run when an image is uploaded to the source bucket. The S3 trigger invokes the function every time an object is created in the bucket. Configure the trigger only on the source bucket. A function that creates objects in the bucket that invokes it can be invoked continuously in a loop, and this is the case when the trigger is on the destination of the function's output. A continuous invocation loop can result in unexpected charges to the AWS account. Using the same S3 bucket for input and output is therefore not recommended.

The Lambda console automatically creates a resource-based policy when a trigger is created. A resource-based policy statement gives other AWS services permission to invoke the function. If you use the CLI, the aws lambda add-permission command gives Amazon S3 permission to invoke the function. This policy statement must exist before the notification configuration, which sends a notification to the function every time a new object is added. The resource-based policy allows Amazon S3 to invoke the function only for actions on the source bucket. It is best practice to specify that the bucket must belong to your account in resource-based policies, because if a bucket is deleted, another AWS account can create a bucket with the same ARN.

## Test the function

A Lambda event is a JSON-formatted document containing data for the function to process. The event sent by S3 contains the bucket name, bucket ARN, and object key.

First, run the dummy event test, which is run before testing by uploading an image and requires the test image to be in the source bucket already. Invocation type RequestResponse invokes the function synchronously. The cli-binary-format option is required with version 2 of the AWS CLI. The destination bucket contains a resized image after the dummy event test only when both the RequestResponse invocation type and the cli-binary-format option are used.

Then test by uploading an image. The Lambda function is automatically invoked when an image is added to the source bucket, but only when the trigger is configured (A trigger must be configured), the trigger invokes the function every time an object is created, and the trigger is configured only on the source bucket. This test comes after the dummy event test. After both tests, the destination bucket contains two resized files.

Deleting unused AWS resources prevents unnecessary charges.

# Tutorial: Creating a Thumbnail with an Amazon S3-Triggered Lambda Function

## Overview

Amazon S3 invokes the Lambda Event Function when an image file is added to the source bucket. The function creates a thumbnail version of the image and outputs it to a different Amazon S3 bucket. The tutorial can be completed using the AWS CLI or the AWS Management Console. The Lambda Event Function can be written in Python or Node.js.

## Prerequisites

The tutorial requires a command line terminal or shell to run commands. Some Bash CLI commands, such as zip, are not supported by Windows built-in terminals. The Windows Subsystem for Linux provides a Windows-integrated version of Ubuntu and Bash, which can be used instead.

## Buckets

The source bucket is the bucket that images are uploaded to. The destination bucket stores the resized thumbnail. The source bucket name must be globally unique and must follow Amazon S3 bucket naming rules, which allow bucket names to contain only lower case letters, numbers, dots, and hyphens. The destination bucket name must be the source bucket name followed by -resized.

The Lambda Event Function must be created in the same AWS Region as the source bucket, and the destination bucket must also be created in that Region. The source bucket needs to contain a test image to confirm the function operates correctly. The test image can be any JPG or PNG file.

## Permissions

An execution role is an IAM role that grants a Lambda Event Function permission to access AWS services and resources. The permissions policy, which is attached to the execution role, gives the function read and write permissions for Amazon S3 buckets and allows it to write to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The trust policy gives the service principal lambda.amazonaws.com permission to call sts:AssumeRole, which allows Lambda to use the role's permissions.

## The Deployment Package

A deployment package contains the function code and its dependencies. The function code uses a separate library for image resizing.

**Node.js.** The function uses the sharp library. The latest version of sharp (0.33) is not compatible with Lambda, so version 0.32.6 should be installed for this tutorial. The function sets the thumbnail width to 200 pixels, and the resize operation sets the height automatically to maintain aspect ratio. The function only supports jpg and png image types; when the image type is unsupported, it returns without resizing.

**Python.** The function uses the Pillow library, which contains C/C++ code. The pip options --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 and --only-binary=:all: install Pillow with pre-compiled binaries compatible with Amazon Linux 2. These pre-compiled binaries make the deployment package work in the Lambda execution environment regardless of the local build machine's OS and architecture. The Lambda Python runtime includes a version of the Boto3 SDK, but it is still recommended to add all function dependencies to the deployment package, even those included in the runtime.

In either case, the files and dependency folders must be at the root of the .zip file.

## Creating the Function

The Lambda console creates a basic Hello world function first, and the code is then replaced by uploading the .zip file. The function is named CreateThumbnail, uses the x86_64 architecture, and uses the LambdaS3Role execution role.

## Configuring the Trigger

A trigger must be configured for the function to run when an image is uploaded to the source bucket. The S3 trigger invokes the function every time an object is created in the bucket. The trigger should be configured only on the source bucket. A function that creates objects in the bucket that invokes it can be invoked continuously in a loop, and such a loop can result in unexpected charges to the AWS account. For this reason, using the same S3 bucket for input and output is not recommended.

The Lambda console automatically creates a resource-based policy when a trigger is created. A resource-based policy statement gives other AWS services permission to invoke the function. When using the CLI instead, the aws lambda add-permission command gives Amazon S3 permission to invoke the function. The resource-based policy allows Amazon S3 to invoke the function only for actions on the source bucket. It is best practice to specify in resource-based policies that the bucket must belong to your account, because if a bucket is deleted, another AWS account can create a bucket with the same ARN. The notification configuration sends a notification to the function every time a new object is added.

## Testing

A Lambda event is a JSON-formatted document containing data for the function to process. The event sent by S3 contains the bucket name, bucket ARN, and object key. The dummy event test is run before testing by uploading an image. Invocation type RequestResponse invokes the function synchronously. The cli-binary-format option is required with version 2 of the AWS CLI. After the dummy event test, the destination bucket contains a resized image.

For the second test, the Lambda function is automatically invoked when an image is added to the source bucket. After both tests, the destination bucket contains two resized files.

## Cleanup

Deleting unused AWS resources prevents unnecessary charges.

# Create a thumbnail with an Amazon S3 trigger for a Lambda function

## Before you begin

- **AWS CLI installed (if using the CLI).** Follow the installation steps at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html.
- **Language support tools and a package manager for your chosen function language.** Install Node.js and npm if you write the function in Node.js, or Python and pip if you write it in Python.

## Overview

When an image file is added to the source bucket, Amazon S3 invokes the Lambda Event Function. The function creates a thumbnail version of the image and outputs it to a different Amazon S3 bucket. You can complete this tutorial using the AWS CLI or the AWS Management Console. The function can be written in Python or Node.js.

The tutorial requires a command line terminal or shell to run commands. Some Bash CLI commands, such as zip, are not supported by Windows built-in terminals. Because of this, the Windows Subsystem for Linux, which provides a Windows-integrated version of Ubuntu and Bash, is available as an option.

## Create the buckets

The source bucket is the bucket that images are uploaded to. It holds only if its name is globally unique, follows Amazon S3 bucket naming rules, and contains only lower case letters, numbers, dots, and hyphens. The destination bucket stores the resized thumbnail. It holds only if the source bucket exists and its name is the source bucket name followed by -resized.

The thumbnail creation works only if the source bucket exists, the destination bucket is created in the same AWS Region as the source bucket, and the Lambda Event Function is created in that same Region as well.

The source bucket needs to contain a test image to confirm the function operates correctly. The test image can be any JPG or PNG file. Upload it before you run the dummy event test.

## Create the execution role

An execution role is an IAM role that grants a Lambda Event Function permission to access AWS services and resources. Create the role first, because the permissions policy is attached to it, and the policy must be attached before the function can use the LambdaS3Role execution role.

The permissions policy gives the function read and write permissions for Amazon S3 buckets and allows the function to write to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The trust policy gives the service principal lambda.amazonaws.com permission to call sts:AssumeRole, which allows Lambda to use the role's permissions.

## Create the deployment package

A deployment package contains the function code and its dependencies. Create it before the Lambda console step, in which a basic Hello world function is created first and its code is then replaced by uploading the .zip file. The files and dependency folders must be at the root of the .zip file.

The function code uses a separate library for image resizing.

**Node.js.** The function uses the sharp library. The latest version of sharp (0.33) is not compatible with Lambda, so install version 0.32.6 for this tutorial. The function sets the thumbnail width to 200 pixels, and the resize operation sets the height automatically to maintain aspect ratio. The function only supports jpg and png image types, so it returns without resizing when the image type is unsupported.

**Python.** The function uses the Pillow library, which contains C/C++ code. The pip options --platform manylinux2014_x86_64 and --only-binary=:all: install Pillow with pre-compiled binaries compatible with Amazon Linux 2. Only with those binaries does the deployment package work in the Lambda execution environment, regardless of the local build machine's OS and architecture. The Lambda Python runtime includes a version of the Boto3 SDK. Even so, it is recommended to add all function dependencies to the deployment package.

## Create the function

Name the function CreateThumbnail, use the x86_64 architecture, and use the LambdaS3Role execution role.

## Configure the Amazon S3 trigger

A trigger must be configured for the function to run when an image is uploaded to the source bucket. The S3 trigger invokes the function every time an object is created in the bucket. Configure the trigger only on the source bucket. A function that creates objects in the bucket that invokes it can be invoked continuously in a loop, which can result in unexpected charges to the AWS account. For that reason, using the same S3 bucket for input and output is not recommended.

The Lambda console automatically creates a resource-based policy when a trigger is created. A resource-based policy statement gives other AWS services permission to invoke the function. With the CLI, the aws lambda add-permission command gives Amazon S3 permission to invoke the function, and so creates that statement. The statement must exist before the notification configuration is set, which sends a notification to the function every time a new object is added. The resource-based policy allows Amazon S3 to invoke the function only for actions on the source bucket. It is best practice to also specify that the bucket must belong to your account, because if a bucket is deleted, another AWS account can create a bucket with the same ARN.

## Test the function

A Lambda event is a JSON-formatted document containing data for the function to process. The event sent by S3 contains the bucket name, bucket ARN, and object key.

First, run the dummy event test, before testing by uploading an image. Invocation type RequestResponse invokes the function synchronously. The cli-binary-format option is required with version 2 of the AWS CLI. The destination bucket contains a resized image after the dummy event test only if both the RequestResponse invocation type and the cli-binary-format option are used.

Then test by uploading an image to the source bucket. The Lambda function is automatically invoked when an image is added to the source bucket, but only when the trigger is configured (a trigger that fires on every object creation) and configured only on the source bucket. This also comes after the dummy event test. After both tests, the destination bucket contains two resized files.

## Clean up

Deleting unused AWS resources prevents unnecessary charges.
